title: Limitations and reproducibility
section: Limitations and deviations from protocol v2
text:
Limitations and deviations from protocol v2

The seven-trial primary set includes one contrast-based trial and one subgroup-derived trial (APROCCHSS CAP subgroup, shock-only, 96% ventilated). The agent hierarchy has two populated clusters and agent is confounded with trial.
Heterogeneity (τ) and the agent SD (ω) are weakly identified; results depend on their half-Normal priors, as the sensitivity grid shows.
Model fitting uses cmdstanr (hybrid likelihood) because brms cannot combine a binomial and a contrast likelihood under one shared effect; brms reproduces the Stan results for the pure-count and pure-contrast cases (cross-check above). The protocol text names brms, so this is a documented deviation.
Sensitivity fits S-vi, S-viii and S-ix were added after protocol v2 (decisions logged 16 to 27 October 2026); S-ix and the SONIA agent-mix rule still need to be written into the registered text.
The one-dimensional tipping analysis reports where P(OR<1) falls below 0.90 and 0.80; an earlier draft of the protocol used different criteria.
RoB 2 is pending and GRADE is not done. The Pitre 2025 values are transcribed from the main text only and need human verification against the PDF and supplement.

title: Model checking
text:
Cross-check against brms
To confirm that the Stan hybrid model reproduces standard software when one likelihood is switched off, each case was refitted in brms (cmdstanr backend, same priors, 4 chains with 2000 post-warmup draws, adapt_delta 0.99):

Pure-count: F1 and F4 with the REMAP-CAP contrast removed, events | trials(n) ~ 0 + trial + trt + (0 + trt | trial) (unpooled trial baselines; trt is the pooled log-OR and the random-slope SD is τ).
Pure-contrast: the S-iii rows for F1 and F4 (every trial as log-OR and SE; Hagman, a double-zero trial, is dropped in F4), yi | se(sei) ~ 1 + (1 | trial).

Agreement was judged against a criterion fixed before looking at the results, in units of the pooled posterior SD of each quantity: means and medians within 0.10 SD and 2.5% and 97.5% quantiles within 0.20 SD (Monte Carlo error alone is of the order 0.02 to 0.05 SD, larger in the tails). It was assessed for μ, τ and every shrunken trial effect θ.

xc |> group_by(Comparison = comparison) |>
  summarise(Parameters = n(), `All within criterion` = all(agree),
            `Max |mean diff| (SD)` = round(max(abs(d_mean_sd)), 3), `Max |median diff| (SD)` = round(max(abs(d_median_sd)), 3),
            `Max |2.5% diff| (SD)` = round(max(abs(d_q025_sd)), 3), `Max |97.5% diff| (SD)` = round(max(abs(d_q975_sd)), 3),

title: Model checking
text:
Leave-one-trial-out and pooled-baseline comparison
PSIS-LOO is not reliable for this model: for F1, Pareto k exceeds 0.7 for 14 of 18 arm-level and trial-level terms, because each unpooled baseline is identified only by its own trial. Exact leave-one-trial-out refits were used instead, scoring the held-out treatment arm given its control arm (the contrast for REMAP-CAP), for both the primary unpooled-baseline model and a pooled-baseline comparison model.

  left_join(distinct(mortality, trial_id, study_label), by = c("trial" = "trial_id")) |>
  transmute(`Held-out trial` = study_label, `Unpooled baselines` = round(unpooled, 2), `Pooled baselines` = round(pooled, 2),

Code

Across the 12 F1 sensitivity fits the posterior median OR ranges from 0.60 to 0.74 and P(OR<1) from 0.84 to 0.98, against 0.68 and 0.95 for the default.

S-ii (low risk of bias only) has not been run: RoB 2 judgements are pending for all trials, so the code is a stub that stops until they are supplied.
S-iii converts each count trial to a log-OR and SE, adding 0.5 to all four cells of any trial with a zero cell (Confalonieri) and dropping double-zero trials. It is the only fit that uses a continuity correction; the forest plot on the results page also adds 0.5 to Confalonieri’s raw estimate, for display only.
S-iv varies the τ prior (half-Normal SD 0.25 and 1) and, in the agent model, the ω prior (SD 0.5).
S-v uses a tighter baseline prior, Normal(0, 2), instead of Normal(0, 10).
S-vi, S-viii and S-ix drop the subgroup-derived trial (APROCCHSS; in F4 also Tongyoo), the mineralocorticoid trial (APROCCHSS) and the single-bolus short-course trial (Marik).
S-IPD replaces rank-1 rows with Smit 2025 IPD rank-2 rows (cross-check only; never merged with the rank-1 row for the same trial).

D1 (ESCAPe short-term row). Default is in-hospital (protocol field 24: earliest of in-hospital, 28-day, 30-day), which leans toward harm. The project status log lists the trial’s d60 row, so the default and the log differ. The pooled result moves from P(OR<1) = 0.95 (default) to 0.97 (d60) and 0.97 (IPD 30-day).
D2 (REMAP-CAP in the short-term fit). There is no valid short-term contrast; the d90 pooled contrast is used by default. Excluding REMAP-CAP gives P(OR<1) = 0.98. The contrast SE is interim (0.362, from the credible interval), and the result is sensitive to it (SE 0.30 to 0.45: P(OR<1) 0.94 to 0.96).
D3 (prior ladder). The enthusiastic N(log 0.70, 0.20), reference N(0, 1.0) and skeptical N(0, 0.35) rungs are proposals; the mild-harm N(log 1.10, 0.20) and REMAP-CAP-harm N(log 1.50, 0.35) rungs are protocol-fixed. Sign-off needed on centre and SD of the first three.
D4 (τ and ω hyperpriors). Primary τ ~ half-Normal(0, 0.5) and ω ~ half-Normal(0, 0.25) are proposals; the sensitivity grid is reported below.

Choices not on the D1–D4 list that also need confirmation

Meta-regression coefficient prior b ~ Normal(0, 1), applied to covariates centred and (for continuous ones) scaled to SD 1.
Pooled-baseline comparison model: a0 ~ Normal(0, 2), sigma_a ~ half-Normal(0, 1) (comparison only; primary baselines stay unpooled).

text:
At a glance
For the primary short-term fit (F1: seven severe-CAP trials, reference prior), the pooled odds ratio is 0.68 (0.38–1.10) with P(OR<1) = 0.95. This is the pre-specified default; see the alternatives above and the pages below before relying on it.

Methods: model, fits and sampling.

Meta-regression.

title: Methods
text:
Model and sampling

Model. One-stage random-effects model on the log-OR with a hybrid likelihood: exact binomial for count trials and a normal likelihood for REMAP-CAP, which enters only as an adjusted contrast (log-OR 0.445, SE 0.362). Trial baselines are unpooled fixed effects with an N(0, 10) prior. Implemented in Stan (stan/hybrid_ma.stan) via cmdstanr; the protocol text names brms, so this is a documented deviation.
Fits. F1 primary short-term (7 trials), F2 90-day (3), F3 broad-severe (10), F4 all-hospitalised (17); F1 with an agent hierarchy; prior ladder; tipping-point analyses; sensitivity fits; meta-regressions.
Sampling. 4 chains × 2000 post-warmup draws, adapt_delta 0.99, max_treedepth 12, seed 7291. A fit is accepted only if R-hat < 1.01, bulk and tail ESS > 400 and there are zero divergences.
Priors. Pooled log-OR μ: Normal(0, 1) in the main fits (the reference rung), with the alternatives on the prior ladder page; between-trial SD τ ~ half-Normal(0, 0.5); between-agent SD ω ~ half-Normal(0, 0.25); trial baselines Normal(0, 10). The sensitivity page varies τ, ω and the baseline prior.
Quantities. Posterior median OR with a 95% quantile credible interval (CrI; HDI columns are in the downloadable tables), P(OR<1), P(OR<0.9), P(OR<0.833), P(OR>1.1), τ, the predictive OR for a new trial, and the absolute risk reduction (ARR) and number needed to treat (NNT). OR < 0.833 (= 1/1.2) corresponds to at least a 20% reduction in the odds of death, the futility threshold used in REMAP-CAP.

title: Methods
text:
Abbreviations
CrI: credible interval; OR: odds ratio; RR: risk ratio; ARR: absolute risk reduction; NNT: number needed to treat; ESS: effective sample size; ELPD: expected log predictive density; IPD: individual patient data; RoB 2: Cochrane risk-of-bias tool, version 2; PSI: Pneumonia Severity Index.

text:
Prior ladder
The ladder places a sequence of priors on the pooled log-OR. The mild-harm and REMAP-CAP-harm rungs are fixed by the protocol; the other three are proposals awaiting confirmation. Each regression fits \(\theta_k = \mu + b\,x_k + u_k\) with covariates centred (continuous ones also scaled to SD 1, so \(b\) is per SD; for binary covariates \(b\) is the difference between groups). A covariate is fitted only if at least four trials have data and it varies. These are across-trial, ecological analyses with very few trials; they are underpowered and not confirmatory.


Code
mr_fit <- filter(mr, status == "fitted")
n_excl0 <- sum(mr_fit$b_q025 > 0 | mr_fit$b_q975 < 0)


22 regressions were fitted and 1 has a 95% credible interval that excludes zero. With this many regressions, about one interval in twenty would be expected to exclude zero by chance, so none of these results should be read as confirmatory.

title: Benchmark against Pitre 2025
text:
Code
library(targets)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)




Code
source("_helpers.R")




Code
pitre_bench <- tar_read(pitre_bench)
pitre <- tar_read(pitre_tbl)


Pitre et al. (Intensive Care Med 2025;51:917-929, DOI 10.1007/s00134-025-07912-2) is the closest prior synthesis: 30 randomised trials in adults hospitalised with non-viral CAP (22 labelled severe CAP), pairwise, Bayesian and dose-response analyses. The values below were transcribed from the open-access full text on PubMed Central into pitre2025_reported.csv (with section or table for each value) and should be checked by a human against the PDF. The supplement (including Table S2, which holds the Bayesian priors) was not examined.


Code

  transmute(Source = source, Trials = dash(trials), Patients = dash(patients), Measure = measure,
            `Estimate (95% interval)` = or_ci(estimate, lo, hi, 2), `P(OR<0.9)` = ifelse(is.na(P_OR_lt_0.9), "", pr(P_OR_lt_0.9)),
            `Control risk` = pr(control_risk, 3),
            `Absolute effect per 1000 (95% interval)` = ifelse(is.na(abs_per_1000), "", sprintf("%+.0f (%+.0f to %+.0f)", abs_per_1000, abs_lo, abs_hi))) |>
  kable(caption = "Benchmark against Pitre 2025. Negative absolute effects mean fewer deaths with corticosteroids; for our fits they are the absolute risk reduction at the pooled control risk of that set.")

How to read the comparison:

Effect scale. Pitre reports a risk ratio. The second row converts it to an odds ratio at their stated control risk of 17.5% with \(OR = RR(1-p)/(1-RR\,p)\); this is our approximation and is not a value reported by the paper.
Time horizon and set. Pitre’s short-term mortality is described inconsistently in the paper (28 to 30 days in the abstract, “up to 60 days” in the methods, “30 to 60 days” in Table 2) and covers 29 trials; our F4 (17 trials) is the nearest set in scope, and F1 is the severe-only set. Patient numbers for our fits count only trials with arm-level counts, so the REMAP-CAP contrast trial adds none.
No severe-only comparator. The main text of Pitre gives trial counts for severe CAP but no severe-only mortality estimate, so F1 cannot be compared like for like. The posterior OR and credible interval for their Bayesian analysis are also not reported in the main text, only P(OR<0.9) = 0.868.
Estimates. Our F4 OR is 0.74 (0.55–0.95), against 0.79 (0.70–0.89) for the converted Pitre estimate.
Probability of OR below 0.9. For our F1, F3 and F4 it is 0.89, 0.88 and 0.94, against 0.87 for Pitre.

The trial sets, scales, weights and priors all differ, so this is a face-validity check, not a replication.
